blueprint_refs: simulation_evaluation.metrics names: train_loss/val_loss/test_loss vs io_contract naming

evidence.metrics: Code writes metrics keys: train_loss/val_loss/test_loss etc; Blueprint io_contract expects train_mse_overall/val_mse_overall/test_mse_overall and conservation_violation_rate.

results-json-schema-mismatch.error_identification: The produced results.json does not follow the BLUEPRINT io_contract metric key schema, which can break downstream evaluation even if simulation is correct.
results-json-schema-mismatch.root_cause_analysis: Evaluator.compute_metrics emits non-contract keys (train_loss, val_loss, test_loss, val_conservation_violation_rate). save_results writes these verbatim instead of mapping to the required io_contract keys.
results-json-schema-mismatch.correct_approach: In Evaluator.compute_metrics and/or save_results, add a contract-mapping layer: output both (a) the current keys for internal prints and (b) the exact BLUEPRINT-required keys in results.json: train_mse_overall, val_mse_overall, test_mse_overall, val_mse_S/I/R, conservation_violation_rate. Keep val_predicted_mean_trajectories.csv unchanged.
results-json-schema-mismatch.key_insight: Always separate internal metric naming from required IO contract: implement an explicit schema adapter before writing artifacts.

blueprint_refs: execution step 4: evaluate on full train/val/test sets without any additional temporal holdout split

evidence.metrics: holdout_split is computed but ignored in SBINPECalibrator.fit (assigned to _). This is dead logic that conflicts with blueprint intent.

improper-holdout-split-present.error_identification: A temporal holdout split is implemented despite the blueprint explicitly requiring no within-trajectory time split; it is currently unused, creating confusion and increasing risk of future leakage/incorrect evaluation changes.
improper-holdout-split-present.root_cause_analysis: holdout_split() implements a prefix/suffix split and main() passes it into calibrator.fit, but SBINPECalibrator.fit discards it. This contradicts the blueprint and makes future modifications error-prone.
improper-holdout-split-present.correct_approach: Remove holdout_split entirely from main flow, or repurpose HoldoutBundle into a no-op placeholder that matches the blueprint (e.g., store only metadata). Ensure calibrator.fit signature and callers reflect that calibration uses the full observed trajectory_id==0.
improper-holdout-split-present.key_insight: If the spec forbids an evaluation split, delete the split machinery; unused code is a common source of accidental leakage later.

blueprint_refs: initialization: Random seed optionally set for reproducibility (not mandatory determinism)
execution: SBI calibration via NPE (training stability important)

evidence.metrics: Validation loss remains high (val_loss=280.22) and does not improve beyond prior run; forcing torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True) can degrade performance/compatibility and slow training, reducing effective optimization.

deterministic-algorithms-enabled-hurting.error_identification: SBI training may be unnecessarily constrained and potentially suboptimal due to enforcing deterministic algorithms globally.
deterministic-algorithms-enabled-hurting.root_cause_analysis: set_global_seed() calls torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True) unconditionally. For SBI neural density estimation, this can disable faster kernels and sometimes changes numerics/optimizer behavior, reducing convergence quality for a fixed epoch budget.
deterministic-algorithms-enabled-hurting.correct_approach: Make deterministic algorithms optional via CLI flag (default off). Keep seeding (random/np/torch manual_seed) for reproducibility, but do not force deterministic algorithms unless explicitly requested. Log whether determinism is enabled.
deterministic-algorithms-enabled-hurting.key_insight: Reproducibility is seeding; determinism is a stronger constraint that can harm model training—make it opt-in, not default.

blueprint_refs: execution step 3: flatten full (T+1)x3 trajectory as x for NPE
objective: infer parameters from a single observed trajectory (trajectory_id=0 only)

evidence.metrics: Large generalization gap and high errors: train_loss=186.36 vs val_loss=280.22; per-dim val S and R errors dominate (val_loss_per_dim.S=415.54, R=334.11) while I is much lower (91.01).

single-trajectory-sbi-summary-too-high-d.error_identification: Posterior inference from a single flattened 183-dim observation appears to overfit/noise-fit and does not transfer to other trajectories; validation and test losses remain high.
single-trajectory-sbi-summary-too-high-d.root_cause_analysis: SBINPECalibrator.fit uses the raw flattened trajectory as the observation/simulation output vector (dimension 183). With only 2000 simulations and a flexible density estimator, NPE can struggle to learn a stable inverse mapping, especially when many dimensions are redundant (S and R are deterministically tied to I via conservation) and scales differ. This reduces posterior quality, harming cross-trajectory performance.
single-trajectory-sbi-summary-too-high-d.correct_approach: Keep blueprint-compatible flattening but improve identifiability and conditioning by changing the observation representation inside SBINPECalibrator.fit before feeding into NPE: (1) standardize/normalize x using z-score computed over simulated xs (fit scaler on xs, apply to x_o); (2) optionally reduce redundancy by transforming x from (S,I,R) to (I,R) or (S,I) while still remaining a flattening of the trajectory (still a flattened full trajectory, just of fewer compartments); (3) weight time steps (e.g., emphasize early growth/peak window) by multiplying x dimensions with a fixed taper to improve parameter sensitivity. Ensure the same transform is applied to all simulated xs and x_o.
single-trajectory-sbi-summary-too-high-d.key_insight: When using NPE on a single long trajectory, always normalize and remove redundant dimensions; otherwise the density estimator learns scale artifacts instead of parameter-sensitive structure.

blueprint_refs: initialization: Random seed optionally set for reproducibility
comparison_method: run K stochastic rollouts per trajectory and output mean

evidence.metrics: Metrics are stable but potentially biased/low-variance due to reusing the same numpy Generator for (a) SBI simulation generation and (b) evaluation rollouts; this can reduce effective randomness in posterior training and evaluation.

rng-reuse-couples-sbi-and-evaluation-rol.error_identification: Using the same RNG stream for SBI training simulations and later evaluation can introduce unintended coupling and reduce the reliability of validation estimates.
rng-reuse-couples-sbi-and-evaluation-rol.root_cause_analysis: main() creates a single rng = default_rng(seed) and passes it into SBINPECalibrator and also into DiscreteTimeSIRSimulator for evaluation. SBINPECalibrator.fit consumes many random draws, advancing the RNG state; evaluation then depends on training consumption order.
rng-reuse-couples-sbi-and-evaluation-rol.correct_approach: Derive independent RNG streams: in main(), create rng_sbi and rng_eval by splitting the seed (e.g., using SeedSequence.spawn or initializing two Generators with different seeds derived from cfg.seed). Use rng_sbi for SBI simulation generation and rng_eval for evaluation rollouts. Optionally create per-trajectory child RNGs to avoid order-dependence across trajectories.
rng-reuse-couples-sbi-and-evaluation-rol.key_insight: Never reuse a single RNG stream across training and evaluation; split RNGs to prevent order-dependent randomness affecting validation.

blueprint_refs: io_contract: relies on dataset files under provided data directory; does not require absolute path constraint

evidence.metrics: No crash in current run, but load_data enforces DATA_DIR must be absolute, which is not required by blueprint and can cause runtime failures in other environments.

hard-requirement-absolute-data-dir.error_identification: Unnecessary restriction can cause avoidable runtime errors when DATA_DIR is relative.
hard-requirement-absolute-data-dir.root_cause_analysis: load_data() raises ValueError if data_dir is not absolute, even though main constructs data_dir from PROJECT_ROOT + DATA_PATH and could be relative depending on env setup.
hard-requirement-absolute-data-dir.correct_approach: Remove the absolute-path check; instead, normalize with os.path.abspath and proceed. Keep existence checks for directory/files.
hard-requirement-absolute-data-dir.key_insight: Avoid adding path format constraints not required by the spec; normalize paths instead of rejecting them.
